title: Mitigating Resource Usage Dependency in Sorting-based KV Stores on Hybrid Storage Devices via Operation Decoupling
problem: Sorting-based key-value stores (LSM-tree based) on hybrid storage experience tight coupling where concurrent operations—background compaction, foreground writes, and reads—compete for the same DRAM cache and I/O bandwidth, creating resource dependencies that limit throughput and predictability.
motivation: Hybrid storage systems combining DRAM and SSDs are ubiquitous in modern data centers, but tightly coupled operations waste bandwidth and cause performance degradation under concurrent mixed workloads.
method: The system decouples operations by giving compaction (the background process that reorganizes data in LSM-tree structures), writes, and reads their own separate memory pools so they don't fight over DRAM cache. It also assigns each operation type distinct I/O scheduling rules—separate policies controlling which operation gets to transfer data between memory and hybrid storage (the mix of different-speed storage devices) at any moment. This works because when operations aren't competing for the same resources, each can run efficiently without being blocked or slowed down by the others.
key_novelty: The core innovation is isolating background data reorganization (compaction) from foreground reads and writes by giving each operation type its own memory pool and I/O scheduling in LSM-tree key-value stores on hybrid storage.
contributions: Operation decoupling framework that isolates resource demands between operation types
Independent scheduling policies for compaction, writes, and reads to minimize interference
Improved throughput and reduced latency tail under concurrent workloads
Evaluation demonstrating significant speedups over coupled KV store baselines
primary_theme: Decoupled operations in hybrid-storage key-value systems
